items.title: Z.ai shipped GLM-5.3-Flash openly
items.oneliner: Z.ai released a 1M-context MIT model with 320B total parameters; open multimodal competition just got cheaper and more geopolitical.

items.title: Google shipped Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
items.oneliner: Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe targets noisy, multi-speaker audio, pushing speech products closer to production without custom post-processing.

items.title: Google expanded Gemini video generation
items.oneliner: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash now extends scenes to 40 seconds, making API-first video generation more usable for real products.

items.title: Anthropic proposed a hardware control standard
items.oneliner: Anthropic says Model Hardware Standard cuts lab-device integration from weeks to minutes; agents are moving off screens and into equipment.

items.title: Trail of Bits challenged VM containment
items.oneliner: Trail of Bits argues cyber-capable agents can escape QEMU-KVM sandboxes, which makes VM-only containment look dangerously outdated.

items.title: Gzip exposed another memory safety failure
items.oneliner: CVE-2026-41992 in gzip is another out-of-bounds read in C, reinforcing that memory safety is still an infrastructure problem.

items.title: FFmpeg got fuzzed into a crash
items.oneliner: A vibecoded fuzzer found a division-by-zero bug in FFmpeg, showing cheap automated fuzzing is now table stakes.

items.title: SourceHut tightened its LLM rules
items.oneliner: SourceHut changed its terms after AI projects drove costs and outages, a blunt reminder that agent workloads are not free.

items.title: Nvidia moved to buy Hugging Face
items.oneliner: Nvidia's reported $13B Hugging Face deal would pull the AI developer commons deeper into one compute vendor's orbit.

items.title: Cloudflare cut DNS cache memory hard
items.oneliner: Cloudflare saved 100TB of RAM on 1.1.1.1 while improving throughput 43%; systems work still beats model hype.
